newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece's Metka posts strong H1,sees good prospects.
newsitem.headline: Greece's Metka posts strong H1,sees good prospects.

text.p: Mechanical construction and engineering firm Metka said its first half pretax earnings rose 45.6 percent to 775 million drachma ($3.2 million) on turnover growth of 40.3 percent at 8.672 billion.

"Metka's orderbook of signed contracts on September 11 stands at 28 billion drachmas. These projects will assure full capacity for 1997 but additional works are expected," board chairman Alexandros Koukolis told reporters.
"As it stands, 1997 will be another good year like 1996," he said. ($ = 240.7 Greek Drachma)
Conservative estimates see 1996 pretax profit at 1.6 billion drachmas on turnover of at least 15 billion, 18 billion in 1997, company executives said.

Metka's technical capabilities are evidenced by the range of projects it has undertaken so far, including construction of steel towers for the Public Power Corporation (DEH), lignite grinding mills, handling conveyors and parts of hydroelectric power stations.

Along with generator rotors, turbine casings and electrostatic precipitators the company also specialises in heavy ship loading cranes. Presently, its fixed assets have a market value of 25 billion drachmas, executives said.
Metka enjoyed a strong balance sheet with practically no debt, self financing its needs for working capital and investments. Its cash reserves rose 73 percent to 1.63 billion in the first half.
